card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**ABOUT SOTERIA**

Soteria Flexibles is a leading manufacturer of custom short-run flexible plastic packaging, including liners, pouches and specialty films for healthcare, food and industrial customers across the United States and Canada.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Plant Manager runs the Carol Stream manufacturing site day to day and is accountable for its safety, quality, delivery, cost and people results. Reporting to the Vice President and General Manager, this leader owns extrusion, converting, packaging, maintenance and shipping, and turns the business plan into a safe, efficient, on-time plant.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Safety and Environmental:** Own a safety-first culture on every shift, lead incident investigations and corrective actions, and ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA and applicable state and local requirements.

* **Production and Operations:** Direct daily extrusion, converting, packaging, maintenance and shipping operations to meet schedules and customer ship dates across all shifts.

* **Quality:** Maintain quality systems and inspection standards, drive down scrap, rework and customer complaints, and support customer, healthcare and food-contact audits.

* **Continuous Improvement:** Lead lean manufacturing, 5S and standard work, use data to find gaps, and build the case for capital projects.

* **People Leadership:** Lead, coach and develop supervisors and leads, partner with HR on hiring, attendance and employee relations, and communicate goals through shift huddles and tier meetings.

* **Financial Management:** Build and manage the plant budget with Finance, control labor, resin yield, scrap, maintenance and utility costs, and report results to the Vice President and General Manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations or Manufacturing Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience

* 7 or more years of manufacturing leadership experience, including 3 or more years leading a plant, department or multi-shift operation

* Experience in plastics, flexible packaging, film extrusion or converting

* Proven record improving safety, quality, throughput and cost in a union or non-union setting

* Working knowledge of OSHA requirements and safety program management

* Strong financial skills, including budgets, variance analysis and cost control

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ERP/MRP systems

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Hands-on knowledge of blown film extrusion and poly bag converting

* Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt, or equivalent training

* Experience with healthcare or food-contact packaging requirements

* Bilingual in English and Spanish

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS**

* Daily presence on the manufacturing floor; exposure to noise, heat, moving equipment and forklift traffic; PPE required in designated areas

* Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs occasionally

* Availability across shifts, with occasional evening, weekend or extended hours

**BENEFITS**

Soteria offers a challenging and rewarding working environment where employees are encouraged to develop and grow as professionals. The position also offers an excellent compensation package and a comprehensive suite of benefits.

* Medical, dental and vision insurance

* Paid time off and paid holidays

* 401(k) retirement savings plan with a company match

The above description is intended to describe the general content, identify the essential functions, and set forth the requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or requirements.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

Pay: $125,000.00 - $145,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Engineering & Continuous Improvement
card.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.

The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.

The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.

***This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.***

***Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.***

**Position Responsibilities may include, but not limited to**

Process & Technical Engineering

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

**Required Skills and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* **10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams**
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies
* Knowledge of Sanitary Design Principles and Standards for food manufacturing.
* Experience leading teams in regulated manufacturing environments
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional leaders and drive enterprise-wide change

**Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
* Food manufacturing, packaged goods, pharmaceutical, and automated distribution experience
* Experience with Industry 4.0 technologies, predictive maintenance, and digital manufacturing tools
* Experience managing and understanding facility utility controls, including HVAC, water, and steam systems
* Professional Engineer (PE) license or advanced technical degree
 **Physical Requirements**

**Physical Requirements**

* Regularly required to use hands to feel, grab, or operate objects, tools, and controls while reaching with hands and arms
* Frequently required to stand, communicate, and listen
* Occasionally required to walk, stoop, kneel or crouch
* Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
* Visual perception to perform job including peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Able to perform repetitive movements
* Able to work in variable temperatures (cold/hot)

card.description:
**Job Details**
---------------

**Job Title: Director, Quality**

**Location: Meriden, CT**

**Work Arrangement:** Onsite

**About the Role**
------------------

**The Director of Quality** provides leadership, direction, and support to the Quality team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus. This role is responsible for ensuring the safe, compliant, and consistent manufacture, validation, and delivery of chemical products while maintaining the highest standards of quality and operational excellence. As a leader of the Quality Team, the Director coaches, develops, and empowers team members to achieve individual and departmental goals, build technical expertise, and drive continuous improvement across the organization. The Director also ensures timely and effective management of quality-related communications, processes and programs that support both customer satisfaction and business growth. L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

***Job Title:*** ***Senior Manager, Quality Management***

***Job Code: 48241***

***Job Location: Orange, VA***

***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***

**Job Description:**

The **Senior Manager of Quality** will be responsible for leading all aspects of Quality Assurance throughout the product development lifecycle for L3Harris’ Culpeper, VA site. This position will have responsibility for direct supervision and leadership of ~60 quality personnel. The Sr. Manager will be responsible for driving continual process and product improvement ensuring product and process integrity, leading to customer satisfaction and overall mission success while supporting division quality, delivery and cost targets. This position will lead quality personnel and collaborate frequently with Program leadership, Engineering, Manufacturing and Supply Chain personnel. This is a hands-on, highly involved leadership position. Ability to obtain a Secret clearance is required for this position.

**Essential Functions:**

 

* Responsible for the Quality Engineering and Inspection functions, supporting all business practices, including quality planning, compliance monitoring and validation for programs, hardware, software and inspection.
* Responsibility for resolving technical challenges, ensuring successful tactical execution, as well as creating and implementing the strategic vision for the Quality department.
* Develop and implement strategic Quality initiatives and programs in support of the site promoting sound and effective principles as set forth in company procedures, government standards and directives, and commercially proven methodology and ensure that the department conforms to these principles.
* Promote a strong culture of quality focused on every employee engaged and enhancing the customer experience through rigorous attention to detail and prevention of defects.
* Work closely with the program teams and the functional organizations to ensure that all phases of the product life cycle, from early customer involvement through post-delivery support, meet the requirements for mission success.
* Ensure that manufacturing engineering, operations and design engineering interact sufficiently throughout the product planning and design phases to ensure a seamless hand-off during product transition to production including design reviews and facilitating quality concurrent Engineering.
* Responsible for the maintenance of quality records that document the quality status of material/products and provide necessary information and cumulative data for internal and external Customer responses.
* Develop, review and verify compliance of all Work Package Descriptions issued for Quality tasks for proposals and ongoing contracts/projects.
* Improve the efficiency of the Quality organization through effective leadership, individual and group training, and process improvement.
* Collect and analyze key quality measures such as Cost of Poor Quality to develop zero defect plans, improve yields and reduce rework during engineering and manufacturing efforts. Report to senior leadership on business performance including action plans to improve business execution and status of strategic initiatives.
* Maintain certification and compliance efforts for AS9100 and other required certifications.
* Business travel up to 10%.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 12 years of prior related Quality Management experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior related experience.
* Active Secret US Security Clearance.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

 

* In depth knowledge of quality and reliability methods and procedures for hardware and software systems as they apply to the aerospace or electronic industry.
* Greenbelt or Blackbelt certification and/or proven education or work history in leading and implementing projects.
* Experience with Configuration Control management practices.
* ASQ certification preferred; Experience managing AS9100 certified business.
* 5+ years Quality management or operations leadership experience.
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills including communications, facilitation, consulting, coaching, and influencing.
* Self-motivated and possess demonstrated ability to motivate others to achieve timely results.
* Highly collaborative style, capable of working across multiple functional areas to drive results.

This is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as final offer amount may vary based on factors including but not limited to experience and geographic location. The specific programs and options available to an employee may vary depending on date of hire, schedule type, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or other related medical conditions), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, characteristic or membership in any other group protected by federal, state or local laws. L3Harris maintains a drug-free workplace and performs pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where permitted by law.

Please be aware many of our positions require the ability to obtain a security clearance. Security clearances may only be granted to U.S. citizens. In addition, applicants who accept a conditional offer of employment may be subject to government security investigation(s) and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

By submitting your resume for this position, you understand and agree that L3Harris Technologies may share your resume, as well as any other related personal information or documentation you provide, with its subsidiaries and affiliated companies for the purpose of considering you for other available positions.

**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

**Position Summary:**

The **Sr Director Process Engineering Peptides API** sets enterprise direction and senior technical governance for process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing within AbbVie Strategic Investment.

The role supports Strategic Investments through engineering leadership, technical expertise, standards development, technical governance and project execution support across multiple manufacturing sites, strategic investments and technology platforms.

The role supports engineering activities associated with peptides manufacturing facility investments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity creation, advanced manufacturing platforms and new technology deployments across the Strategic Investment portfolio.

The role partners with Strategic Investments, manufacturing sites, operations, quality, EHS, validation / CQV and external engineering partners to deliver technically robust and business-aligned engineering solutions.

**Strategic Investment Context**

* Strategic Investment provides engineering leadership, technical governance, standards development and project execution support across AbbVie’s Strategic Investments and strategic capital portfolio.
* The organization supports new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing facilities, new platform deployments, strategic capacity creation, advanced biologics and CGT manufacturing capabilities and standards development for emerging technologies across Strategic Investments.
* Strategic Investment roles are expected to promote common standards, transfer lessons learned across regions and sites, and enable consistent engineering delivery across strategic capital investments.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Investment Governance and Standards:**

* Establish, maintain and deploy global engineering standards, technical practices and governance expectations for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery.
* Drive consistent application of technical standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Define enterprise standards, engineering requirements and technical guardrails for new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies, including requirements for consistent design, deployment, qualification, operation and scale-up across Strategic Investments.
* Ensure discipline strategies support AbbVie’s long-range Strategic Investment objectives, strategic investment programs and adoption of new technologies across future manufacturing platforms.
* Provide governance and escalation for technical decisions with material safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability or lifecycle impact.

**Strategic New Technology and Capital Investment Support:**

* Provide engineering leadership for strategic capital investments, including new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy facility builds, technology platform deployments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity projects and lifecycle technology upgrades.
* Support front-end engineering, facility concept development, investment option evaluation, manufacturing capability assessments and site / platform planning activities for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy assets.
* Partner with Strategic Investments and project leadership to ensure technical assumptions, deliverables, risks and resource needs are integrated into capital program plans.
* Apply Strategic Investment lessons learned and standards to improve project quality, speed, reliability and readiness across the portfolio.

**Technical Leadership and Delivery:**

* Lead or support technical decision-making for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery across multiple manufacturing sites, capital projects and technology platforms.
* Ensure engineering deliverables support safety, quality, compliance, operability, maintainability, reliability, sustainability and operational readiness.
* Coordinate technical input from project teams, site SMEs, external engineering partners, vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.
* Drive timely resolution of technical issues and ensure suitable escalation when decisions have broader project, network or business impact.

**Cross-Functional Integration:**

* Partner with Strategic Investments, manufacturing operations, quality, validation / CQV, EHS, site engineering, MS&T, supply chain, finance and related engineering disciplines.
* Ensure discipline decisions are integrated with biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing strategy, network capacity, technology platform deployment, regulatory expectations and site handover needs.
* Facilitate collaboration across Strategic Investments, sites and project teams to avoid fragmented solutions and drive consistency across the strategic capital portfolio.
* Represent Strategic Investment in technical reviews, project forums and risk discussions relevant to assigned scope.

**Capability Building and Continuous Improvement:**

* Share engineering best practices, lessons learned and technical knowledge across sites, regions and projects.
* Build capability through coaching, mentoring, technical review discipline and development of reusable engineering practices.
* Promote a culture of engineering excellence, safety, quality, reliability, collaboration, accountability and proactive risk management.
* Support continuous improvement of Strategic Investment standards, templates, knowledge management and project delivery approaches.

**Strategic Investment Leadership Expectations:**

* Collaborate across Strategic Investments to identify, develop and deploy best practices, technical standards, lessons learned and capability-building initiatives.
* Promote consistency, quality, reliability, sustainability and project delivery performance across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Support long-range manufacturing strategy, strategic investment planning and Strategic Investment capability development.
* Build technical capability through coaching, mentoring, standards governance, knowledge management and cross-functional collaboration.

**Stakeholder Interfaces**

card.description:
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Directly Supervises: Executive Operations Coordinator, Administrative Manager, Administrative Assistants, Revenue Cycle Manager, Operations Manager, and other operational employees assigned by the Chief Executive Officer

Schedule: Full-time; 40 hours per week, with scheduling flexibility based on operational needs

Compensation: As stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement

Work Arrangement: Primarily remote, with weekly on-site presence required at Elevation's Homewood and Matteson offices

COMPENSATION AND HOURS

* This is a full-time, salaried-exempt position scheduled for 40 hours per week. The employee will receive the salary stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

* If time reporting is required for attendance, workload, leave, or administrative purposes, the employee must accurately record actual hours worked. Time entries do not change the established salary.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Operations ensures that Elevation Individual & Family Therapy's administrative and operational functions are organized, accountable, compliant, and aligned with client-service and financial goals. The position reduces the CEO's involvement in routine operations by resolving matters within the role's authority, ensuring assigned work is completed, and presenting recommendations when executive approval is required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

1. OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP AND STAFF ACCOUNTABILITY

* Set priorities, deadlines, performance expectations, and coverage plans for assigned staff across both locations.

* Conduct regular supervision meetings and monitor attendance, responsiveness, accuracy, productivity, professionalism, and follow-through.

* Review required reports and promptly address missed deadlines, repeated errors, unresolved concerns, and incomplete work.

* Provide training, coaching, written expectations, and documented corrective feedback; coordinate performance improvement or disciplinary processes with the Executive Operations Coordinator and CEO.

* Assign each operational concern to an appropriate owner, monitor it through resolution, and escalate only matters requiring executive, legal, financial, clinical, or regulatory authority.

2. ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLIENT-SERVICE OPERATIONS

* Oversee phone and voicemail coverage, new-client inquiries, intake follow-up, insurance verification, required paperwork, scheduling, check-in, and appointment confirmation.

* Monitor re-engagement, no-show and cancellation outreach, copay collection, approved payment-plan workflows, and records requests.

* Ensure administrative staff consistently follow approved scripts, workflows, response-time standards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

* Oversee office calendars, room assignments, supplies, equipment, routine facility concerns, and administrative coverage.

* Coordinate with clinical leadership when an operational concern affects client care, provider scheduling, documentation, or referrals.

3. REVENUE CYCLE OVERSIGHT

* Directly supervise the Revenue Cycle Manager, establish performance expectations, review results, provide coaching and accountability, and ensure timely follow-through on revenue-cycle priorities.

* Hold the Revenue Cycle Manager accountable for routine billing operations and supervision of assigned billing staff; coordinate cross-department priorities and escalate unresolved financial, payer, staffing, or compliance risks to the CEO.

* Review reports related to claims, denials, payment posting, insurance follow-up, patient balances, accounts receivable, and collections.

* Ensure billing concerns are assigned, documented, and resolved within established timelines.

* Identify administrative or clinical workflow failures that contribute to denials, delayed billing, inaccurate balances, or lost revenue.

* Coordinate communication among RCM, administrative, clinical, and collections staff and escalate material payer, financial, or compliance concerns.

4. POLICIES, SOPS, AND EHR WORKFLOW IMPROVEMENT

* Identify processes requiring a written policy, SOP, checklist, script, workflow, quality check, or escalation procedure.

* Draft and update operational policies and SOPs with the employees and subject-matter experts responsible for the work; coordinate approval by the appropriate leader.

* Maintain version control, review dates, distribution, training, employee acknowledgment, and monitoring of approved procedures.

* Evaluate EHR and technology workflows for intake, scheduling, documentation tracking, billing, records, client communication, and reporting.

* Identify duplicate entry, inconsistent data, preventable delays, and unnecessary manual work; recommend and coordinate approved templates, reports, alerts, tracking tools, automations, and vendor requests.

* Test approved changes, document the revised workflow, coordinate staff training, and monitor implementation while protecting confidentiality and system access.

5. HR, CREDENTIALING, AND COMPLIANCE COORDINATION

Directly supervise the Executive Operations Coordinator by establishing priorities, monitoring deadlines and accuracy, reviewing performance, and ensuring timely completion of assigned HR administration, credentialing, compliance, records, onboarding, offboarding, and policy-related responsibilities. The Executive Operations Coordinator or other assigned personnel retain responsibility for completing the detailed administrative work and maintaining required records.

* Ensure employee performance, attendance, conduct, onboarding, offboarding, training, personnel documentation, and policy-acknowledgment processes are coordinated appropriately and escalated to the CEO when executive authority or protected reporting is required.

* Review credentialing, recredentialing, payer enrollment, licensure, renewal, training, and compliance trackers; ensure assigned staff follow up on incomplete or at-risk items.

* Coordinate provider status changes with HR, billing, clinical leadership, scheduling, and provider-directory workflows.

* Monitor completion of corrective actions and escalate material delays, expirations, privacy concerns, payer or government inquiries, suspected fraud, client-safety issues, or other significant risks immediately.

* Support audits, internal reviews, payer requests, and corrective-action plans without acting as Elevation's attorney or sole clinical compliance authority.

6. BUDGET AND EXPENSE MONITORING

* Assist the CEO with preparing and monitoring approved administrative and operational budgets.

* Review actual operational expenses against approved amounts, including administrative and billing staffing costs, overtime, office supplies, software subscriptions, vendor charges, and upcoming renewals.

* Identify unusual spending, recurring overages, duplicate services, avoidable expenses, and practical opportunities for cost savings.

* Coordinate with billing and collections personnel to identify preventable revenue leakage related to denials, delayed claims, workflow errors, missed collections, or unresolved client balances.

* Maintain organized records of approved operational purchases and recurring expenses and submit purchase or budget-adjustment requests with the cost, purpose, priority, and recommendation.

* Provide the CEO with a monthly summary of significant budget variances, anticipated expenses, and recommended corrective or cost-saving actions.

7. REPORTING AND LEADERSHIP COLLABORATION

* Provide a concise weekly CEO report covering accomplishments, unresolved matters, staff concerns, revenue cycle issues, credentialing/compliance risks, budget concerns, and policy, SOP, or EHR project status.

* Provide a monthly operational summary identifying trends, recurring problems, performance patterns, completed improvements, and recommended priorities.

* Present significant concerns with relevant facts, actions already taken, and a recommended solution rather than forwarding unorganized information.

* Directly supervise the Administrative Manager and Administrative Assistants. Establish priorities, monitor performance, and maintain formal accountability while using the Administrative Manager's workflow knowledge and assigned functional ownership to support training, quality, office operations, and consistent administrative processes.

8. GROWTH INITIATIVES AND PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

* Lead the operational assessment of CEO-directed growth opportunities, including new services, programs, partnerships, and location expansions. Work with clinical leadership, revenue cycle, and other relevant staff to assess demand, staffing, costs, reimbursement where applicable, space and technology needs, and implementation risks. Clinical leadership guides clinical program design.

* Present the CEO with a recommendation, estimated costs and resources, and a proposed timeline. The CEO decides which opportunities move forward.

* Lead the rollout of approved initiatives. Build the launch plan, assign responsibilities and deadlines, coordinate training and workflow changes, track milestones, and report progress and early results to the CEO.

ROLE BOUNDARIES AND DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY

The Director of Operations owns operational follow-through but does not personally perform every task within the functions overseen. The position may assign and prioritize routine work, require status updates, provide coaching and corrective feedback, implement approved procedures, coordinate across departments, and resolve routine administrative or client-service concerns within established policies.

CEO approval is required before hiring, termination, suspension, compensation changes, material policy changes, unapproved contracts or purchases, new recurring expenses, significant balance waivers, banking or debt decisions, public statements, or substantive responses to legal, government, payer, or regulatory matters. The Director of Operations monitors and recommends but does not replace bookkeeping, payroll, accounting, or executive financial authority.

SCHEDULE AND CAPACITY

* Periodic on-site presence at both Elevation offices is required to observe day-to-day workflows, the office environment, staff performance, client-service operations, and implementation of policies and procedures. The timing and frequency of visits will be based on operational needs and CEO direction.

* The regular schedule will be established by the CEO and will generally total 40 hours per week. Some evening or weekend work may be necessary based on operational needs. The employee must maintain agreed-upon availability during core business hours for supervision, meetings, and time-sensitive matters.

* Continuous after-hours availability is not expected; after-hours contact should generally be limited to urgent matters that cannot reasonably wait. Occasional schedule fluctuations do not change the position's established salary.

* The Director of Operations must notify the CEO when workload or competing priorities cannot reasonably be completed within the established 40-hour schedule and recommend what should be delegated, postponed, or reprioritized.

* Unless otherwise approved, the role should generally carry no more than two major operational improvement projects at one time. Major launches count toward this limit unless the CEO approves an exception.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* At least three years of relevant operations, healthcare administration, office management, or employee-supervision experience.

* Demonstrated ability to supervise employees, address performance concerns, analyze operational data, and independently move work to completion.

* Strong judgment, initiative, organization, problem-solving, discretion, emotional maturity, and written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to draft clear policies, SOPs, reports, checklists, and workflows and to protect confidential client, employee, financial, and business information.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, spreadsheets, cloud-based systems, and the ability to learn and improve EHR and business platforms.

* Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare confidentiality expectations; reliable transportation and ability to work from both Elevation locations as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, management, human resources, or a related field; behavioral health or healthcare operations experience; and experience with revenue cycle, credentialing, compliance, EHR workflow improvement, SOP development, reporting, dashboards, or automations.

card.description:
Overview:

Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger.

The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing daily production activities to drive efficiency, maintain quality, and ensure adherence to company standards. This role leads the development and implementation of organizational strategies, standards, and best practices to achieve world-class operational performance. Additionally, the Director of Production collaborates closely with site and business leadership, leveraging resources and expertise to ensure our products consistently meet customer expectations.

Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Responsibilities:

* Lead with a clear view of where the organization needs to be in 1-3 years; communicates strategic direction to employees and how it fits with the day-to-day actions and results being driven.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Implement and maintain value streams and SCQDCT management system within the site.
* Provide coaching and support to supervisors and frontline employees to enhance skills and performance.
* Set clear and measureable performance expectations, in line with corporate goals; proactively analyze and manage all relative operations performance metrics.
* Provide timely, accurate and complete reports on the operating conditions of the company.Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Ensures alignment with functional leadership (e.g., Engineering, Finance, Quality, Facilities, and Human Resources) on performance management and talent development.
* Ensure the facilities operate within the Company’s ISO and FDA quality management system.
* Participate in the development of the location’s monthly revenue forecasts.
* Monitor and adjust production output and staff levels to support the location’s revenue and cost targets.
* Participate in the development and control of the location’s budgets and quarterly forecasts.
* Working with the senior leadership team, help to develop and implement winning strategies to grow revenues and profitability.
* Ensure the site maintains maximum confidentiality in a highly proprietary operationLead relationship with key intercompany customers to ensure maximum service throughout the value chain.

Required Qualifications:

* BS degree in a technical field, preferably engineering or life sciences.
* Prior experience managing a manufacturing department/organization in a regulated environment.
* Prior experience managing an engineering team.
* Experience working within a Lean, six-sigma organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Prior experience managing an independent manufacturing organization.
* Familiarity with contract manufacturing, ISO and FDA quality system requirements, medical device and diagnostics manufacturing.
* Lean, six-sigma green or black belt certified.
* Experience with Nitinol products and processing
* Experience wit Wire and Tube fabrication
* MBA or relevant business management experience.

Physical Demands:

* Ability to work long hours when necessary and to have a presence with a 24/7 operation.
* Domestic travel required

Compensation:

* The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000–$204,000.
* Our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

Resonetics offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees and their families. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; paid time off (PTO); 10 paid holidays; Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA); life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) insurance; Short-Term Disability (STD) and Long-Term Disability (LTD) insurance; accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance. Eligibility and benefit offerings may vary based on employment status and applicable plan provisions.

We also offer **generous benefits**, such as:

* Dental benefits
* 6 paid holidays
* Flexible scheduling
* PTO
* Leadership and personal development trainings
* A great atmosphere

This is a **full-time position** with a set schedule. If this sounds like the right fit for you, keep reading about this Director of Dental Operations position!

**WANT TO KNOW MORE ABOUT OUR FAMILY-ORIENTED BUSINESS?**

We are a team of highly qualified dentists and specialists who work together to expertly address each of our patients' dental and sedation needs. Our doctors focus their expertise and training on patients who seek only the best in general dentistry and oral surgery. We manage a wide variety of problems relating to the mouth, jaws, and facial region, including bone grafting, wisdom teeth extraction, dental implant surgery, corrective jaw surgery, and traumatic injuries. Our approach to quality dentistry is to customize our care and help our patients meet their goals as we strive to attain total patient satisfaction.

Our staff has been called "caring" in our reviews, which underscores how essential our employees are to our success. To show them how much **we appreciate them and value their contributions**, we provide **flexible scheduling** and offer **highly competitive wages**. We also cultivate a **warm and welcoming atmosphere** that benefits both our patients and our staff. Many people comment that they feel "comfortable" with us, which lets us know we're succeeding at helping **everyone who enters our doors feel at home**.

**DO YOU MEET THESE QUALIFICATIONS?**

* Experience in the dental field with a strong understanding of workflow optimization
* Proactive approach to problem-solving and getting things done
* Ability to guide teams and manage multiple projects effectively
* Comfort in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment
* Problem-solving mindset with a focus on long-term success
* Commitment to enhancing patient care and experiences
* Strong communication skills and a transparent, team-oriented approach
* Passion for continuous learning and leveraging the latest dental technology

**WHAT WILL YOU DO AS A DIRECTOR OF DENTAL OPERATIONS?**

As a Director of Dental Operations, you will play a key role in driving initiatives that support the growth and efficiency of our practice. You will work closely with leadership to turn ideas into action, ensuring that processes run smoothly and effectively. Your day will involve streamlining operations, managing multiple projects, and guiding team members to maintain high standards of care and efficiency. You will thrive in a fast-moving environment where problem-solving and adaptability are essential. From optimizing workflows to implementing innovative solutions, you will make a meaningful impact on both our team and the patients we serve.

If you are excited about this dentistry opportunity and want to be part of a growing dentistry, we'd love to hear from you! Apply today with our 3-minute, mobile-friendly initial application and take the next step in your career!

**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

 

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**

**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**Paid time off**

* Four weeks accrued paid vacation
* Two weeks accrued paid sick leave
* Four mental health days
* Two personal days
* Two floating holidays
* Ten holidays

**Benefits**

* All benefits effective on date of hire with no waiting period
* 100% employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employee-only plans
* 100% employer-paid life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability
* 100% employer-paid downtown Atlanta parking or monthly MARTA card
* Affordable plans for legal insurance, critical illness, supplemental life and more
* Immediate eligibility to contribute to a 403(b), plus a 6% employer-paid contribution after one year regardless of employee contributions
* Cell phone stipend
* Employee Donor Advised Fund after one year
* Employee Assistance Program and more

**Culture, Learning & Development**

* Individual Development Plans with training, resources and development opportunities
* Two wellness rooms with self-care resources
* Monthly employee engagement activities

**TO APPLY**

Submit your resume and cover letter through our Careers website.

Note: Only applications submitted through our website will be accepted. Due to the volume of candidates, we are unable to provide status updates or accommodate phone calls or walk-ins regarding open positions.

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta values diversity and inclusion; we honor the diverse needs, strengths, voices and backgrounds of all individuals in our regional community.

**Director of Operations – DC Restaurant Group**
================================================

**DC Restaurant Group | Richmond VA Area**

**Salary: $150,000–$175,000 Annually**

### **About the Opportunity**

DC Restaurant Group is seeking an experienced and results-driven **Director of Operations** to oversee daily operations across a large restaurant group with multiple locations throughout Virginia and North Carolina.

This is an exciting opportunity for a strong restaurant operations leader who is passionate about developing teams, improving restaurant performance, and driving operational excellence across multiple markets.

The Director of Operations will report directly to the Vice President of Operations and work closely with District Managers to ensure restaurants are operating efficiently, meeting company standards, and achieving financial and operational goals.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily operations across a large portfolio of restaurant locations, ensuring consistency and strong operational performance.
* Lead, coach, and develop District Managers to drive accountability, leadership development, and restaurant success.
* Partner with the Vice President of Operations to execute company strategies, initiatives, and operational goals.
* Monitor restaurant performance, including sales, profitability, labor costs, food costs, and overall P&L results.
* Conduct regular restaurant visits to evaluate operations, identify opportunities for improvement, and support District Managers.
* Ensure restaurants consistently meet company standards for food safety, cleanliness, customer service, and operational efficiency.
* Develop action plans to address performance challenges and improve restaurant results.
* Support recruitment, training, and development of restaurant leadership teams.
* Work closely with District Managers to improve employee retention, guest satisfaction, and overall restaurant performance.
* Provide regular updates to the Vice President of Operations regarding market performance, operational challenges, and opportunities for growth.

### **Qualifications**

* 8+ years of progressive leadership experience in multi-unit restaurant operations.
* Previous experience as a Director of Operations, Regional Director, or senior multi-unit restaurant leader.
* Strong background in quick-service restaurants (QSR), preferably within a franchise or large multi-unit restaurant organization.
* Proven experience leading and developing District Managers across multiple restaurant locations.
* Strong understanding of restaurant financials, P&L management, budgeting, and operational performance.
* Demonstrated success improving restaurant profitability, operational standards, and team performance.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to travel regularly throughout Virginia and North Carolina to support restaurant operations.

### **Compensation**

**$150,000–$175,000 annually**, depending on experience.

**Apply today to join DC Restaurant Group and play a key role in the continued growth and success of our restaurant organization!**

DC Restaurant Group is the corporate headquarters supporting four restaurant brands: Anthony’s Coal Fired Pizza, Burger King (DC Burger), Round Table Pizza, and Buffalo Wild Wings (West Coast Wings). 
Located in Arlington, VA, our corporate office provides support across multiple departments, including Human Resources, Finance, Operations, Facilities, and more. We are continuing to grow our corporate team and are looking for talented individuals to help support our restaurants across multiple states.

Pay: $150000.00 - $175000.00 / year

Benefits:

* Health insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Paid time off

Job Type: fulltime

Education: No education required

Work location: On-site
